title: Field diary: Rani ki Vav, Patan
paragraphs: १४ जनवरी २०२४। सुबह सात बजे हम पाटण पहुँचे। सरस्वती नदी के पुराने किनारे पर स्थित रानी की वाव पहली नज़र में ज़मीन में उतरती एक विशाल सीढ़ी जैसी लगती है। ऊपर से केवल पत्थर की कतारें दिखती हैं, पर नीचे उतरते ही सात मंज़िलों की दीर्घाएँ एक के बाद एक खुलती जाती हैं।

14 January 2024. We reached Patan at seven in the morning. Standing on the old bank of the Saraswati river, Rani ki Vav at first sight looks like a vast staircase descending into the earth. From above you see only rows of stone, but as you go down, galleries on seven levels open up one after another.

स्थानीय गाइड ने बताया कि यह वाव रानी उदयमती ने अपने पति राजा भीमदेव प्रथम की स्मृति में बनवाई थी। परंपरा के अनुसार इसका निर्माण संवत ११२० के आसपास हुआ। दीवारों पर विष्णु के दशावतार, अप्सराएँ और नाग-कन्याएँ उकेरी गई हैं; केवल दूसरी दीर्घा में ही मैंने चालीस से अधिक मूर्तियाँ गिनीं।

The local guide told us that the stepwell was commissioned by Queen Udayamati in memory of her husband, King Bhimdev I. According to tradition it was built around Samvat 1120. The walls are carved with the ten avatars of Vishnu, apsaras and naga maidens; in the second gallery alone I counted more than forty sculptures.

सदियों तक यह वाव नदी की बाढ़ से आई गाद में दबी रही। बीसवीं सदी के उत्तरार्ध में भारतीय पुरातत्व सर्वेक्षण ने इसकी खुदाई और संरक्षण किया, और २०१४ में इसे यूनेस्को विश्व धरोहर घोषित किया गया। शाम को कुंड के पास बैठकर मुझे लगा कि यह स्मारक केवल जल-संग्रह के लिए नहीं, बल्कि एक उलटा मंदिर है।

For centuries the stepwell lay buried under silt brought by the river's floods. In the latter half of the twentieth century the Archaeological Survey of India excavated and conserved it, and in 2014 it was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Sitting by the tank in the evening, I felt that this monument was not built merely to store water, but as an inverted temple.

title: The legend of Rudabai (Gujarati folk tale)
paragraphs: લોકકથા કહે છે કે વાઘેલા રાજા વીરસિંહે ગામ માટે પાણીની વાવ બંધાવવાનું શરૂ કર્યું, પણ કામ પૂરું થાય તે પહેલાં જ યુદ્ધમાં તેમનું મૃત્યુ થયું. તેમની રાણી રૂડાબાઈ શોકમાં ડૂબી ગઈ, છતાં ગામના લોકોને પાણી મળે એ માટે વાવ પૂરી કરવાનો સંકલ્પ તેણે છોડ્યો નહીં.

The folk tale says that the Vaghela king Veer Singh began building a stepwell to bring water to the village, but he was killed in battle before the work was finished. His queen Rudabai was overcome with grief, yet she never gave up her resolve to complete the stepwell so that the people of the village would have water.
વિજેતા સુલતાન મહમૂદ બેગડો રાણીના સૌંદર્યથી મોહિત થયો અને તેણે લગ્નનો પ્રસ્તાવ મૂક્યો. રૂડાબાઈએ એક જ શરત મૂકી: પહેલાં વાવ પૂરી થવી જોઈએ. સુલતાને પોતાના કારીગરો મોકલ્યા અને પાંચ માળની વાવ તૈયાર થઈ.

The victorious Sultan Mahmud Begada was enchanted by the queen's beauty and proposed marriage. Rudabai set a single condition: the stepwell must be completed first. The Sultan sent his own craftsmen, and the five-storey stepwell was finished.

વાવ પૂરી થયા પછી રાણીએ તેની પરિક્રમા કરી અને પાણીમાં કૂદીને પોતાનું વચન અને સન્માન બંને સાચવ્યાં. ગામના વડીલો કહે છે કે આજે પણ ઉનાળાની બપોરે વાવનાં ઠંડાં પગથિયાં પર બેસીએ તો રૂડાબાઈની વાર્તા યાદ આવે છે.

When the stepwell was complete, the queen walked around it and leapt into the water, keeping both her word and her honour. The village elders say that even today, if you sit on the stepwell's cool steps on a summer afternoon, Rudabai's story comes back to you.

title: Field notes: Dada Harir ni Vav, Asarwa
paragraphs: અમદાવાદના અસારવા વિસ્તારમાં આવેલી દાદા હરિરની વાવ સાંકડી ગલીઓ વચ્ચે છુપાયેલી છે. અંદર પ્રવેશતાં જ શહેરનો ઘોંઘાટ ઓછો થઈ જાય છે અને પગથિયાંની લાંબી હાર નીચે અષ્ટકોણ કૂવા સુધી લઈ જાય છે.
Dada Harir's stepwell in the Asarwa area of Ahmedabad is hidden among narrow lanes. As soon as you step inside, the noise of the city fades and a long flight of steps leads down to an octagonal well.
વાવની દીવાલ પર સંસ્કૃત અને અરબી ભાષાના બે શિલાલેખ છે. તેમાં નોંધ છે કે સુલતાન મહમૂદ બેગડાના જનાનખાનાની અધિકારી બાઈ હરિર સુલતાનીએ ઈ.સ. ૧૪૯૯માં આ વાવ બંધાવી હતી. પાસે જ તેમનો મકબરો અને મસ્જિદ પણ છે.

There are two inscriptions on the stepwell's wall, in Sanskrit and Arabic. They record that Bai Harir Sultani, superintendent of Sultan Mahmud Begada's harem, had this stepwell built in 1499 CE. Her tomb and a mosque stand close by.

title: Field notes: Modhera and the patola weavers of Patan
paragraphs: મોઢેરાનું સૂર્ય મંદિર ભીમદેવ પહેલાના સમયમાં ઈ.સ. ૧૦૨૬માં બંધાયું હતું. મંદિરની સામેનો સૂર્યકુંડ પગથિયાંવાળો વિશાળ જળકુંડ છે, જેની ચારે બાજુ નાનાં નાનાં મંદિરો ગોઠવાયેલાં છે. સવારે સૂર્યનાં પહેલાં કિરણો ગર્ભગૃહ સુધી પહોંચે એ રીતે મંદિરની રચના થઈ છે.

The Sun Temple at Modhera was built in 1026 CE in the time of Bhimdev I. The Surya Kund in front of the temple is a vast stepped tank, with small shrines arranged on all four sides. The temple is designed so that the first rays of the morning sun reach the sanctum.

પાટણમાં સાળવી પરિવારના ઘરે અમે પટોળાં વણાતાં જોયાં. તાણા અને વાણા બંનેના દોરા વણાટ પહેલાં જ અલગ અલગ રંગાય છે, તેથી એક સાડી તૈયાર થતાં છ મહિનાથી વધુ સમય લાગે છે. ‘પડી પટોળે ભાત, ફાટે પણ ફીટે નહીં’ એ કહેવત અહીં સૌ જાણે છે.

In Patan, at the home of a Salvi family, we watched patola being woven. The warp and weft threads are both dyed separately before weaving, so a single sari can take more than six months to finish. Everyone here knows the saying: 'the pattern of a patola may tear, but it never fades'.

title: Travel journal: Chand Baori, Abhaneri
paragraphs: आभानेरी गाँव जयपुर-आगरा राजमार्ग से थोड़ा हटकर है। गाँव के बीच में चाँद बावड़ी है, जिसके तीन ओर ज्यामितीय सीढ़ियों का ऐसा जाल है कि आँखें धोखा खा जाती हैं। गाइड के अनुसार इसमें लगभग साढ़े तीन हज़ार सीढ़ियाँ और तेरह मंज़िलें हैं।

Abhaneri village lies a little off the Jaipur–Agra highway. In the middle of the village is Chand Baori, with such a web of geometric steps on three sides that the eye is deceived. According to the guide it has about three and a half thousand steps and thirteen storeys.

कहा जाता है कि इसे नौवीं सदी में निकुंभ वंश के राजा चंदा ने बनवाया था। चौथी ओर बने बहुमंज़िला मंडप में राजपरिवार गर्मियों में ठहरता था, क्योंकि बावड़ी के तल पर तापमान ऊपर की तुलना में कई डिग्री कम रहता है। पास ही हर्षत माता का मंदिर है।

It is said to have been built in the ninth century by King Chanda of the Nikumbha dynasty. The royal family stayed in summer in the multi-storey pavilion on the fourth side, because at the bottom of the stepwell the temperature stays several degrees lower than at the top. The Harshat Mata temple is close by.

title: Stories of Agrasen ki Baoli (Hindi)
paragraphs: कनॉट प्लेस की ऊँची इमारतों के बीच अग्रसेन की बावली एक अलग ही दुनिया है। एक सौ आठ सीढ़ियाँ नीचे उतरती हैं और हर कदम के साथ हवा ठंडी होती जाती है। परंपरा इसे महाराजा अग्रसेन से जोड़ती है, जबकि इसकी वास्तुकला तुगलक या लोदी काल की लगती है।

Amid the tall buildings of Connaught Place, Agrasen ki Baoli is a world of its own. One hundred and eight steps lead down, and the air grows cooler with every step. Tradition links it to Maharaja Agrasen, while its architecture appears to belong to the Tughlaq or Lodi period.

पुरानी दिल्ली के बुज़ुर्ग बताते हैं कि कभी यह बावली काले पानी से भरी रहती थी और लोग शाम के बाद इसके पास जाने से कतराते थे। आज पानी सूख चुका है, पर कहानियाँ अब भी ज़िंदा हैं और कॉलेज के विद्यार्थी यहाँ बैठकर उन्हें दोहराते हैं।

Elders of Old Delhi say that the baoli was once full of black water and that people avoided going near it after dusk. Today the water has dried up, but the stories are still alive, and college students sit here retelling them.

title: Field diary: Toorji ka Jhalra, Jodhpur
paragraphs: जोधपुर के पुराने शहर में मेहरानगढ़ किले की छाया में तुरजी का झालरा है। अठारहवीं सदी में महाराजा अभय सिंह की रानी ने इसे बनवाया था। लाल बलुआ पत्थर पर नक्काशीदार झरोखे और हाथी-मुख वाले जल-निकास देखने लायक हैं।

In Jodhpur's old city, in the shadow of Mehrangarh fort, lies Toorji ka Jhalra. A queen of Maharaja Abhay Singh had it built in the eighteenth century. Its carved balconies and elephant-headed water spouts in red sandstone are well worth seeing.

कई दशकों तक यह झालरा कचरे से भरा रहा। हाल के वर्षों में सफ़ाई और जीर्णोद्धार के बाद यह फिर से शहर का मिलन-स्थल बन गया है। यहाँ बच्चे पानी में छलाँग लगाते हैं और बुज़ुर्ग सीढ़ियों पर बैठकर पुराने दिनों की बातें करते हैं।

For several decades the jhalra was filled with rubbish. After cleaning and restoration in recent years it has once again become a meeting place for the city. Children jump into the water and elders sit on the steps talking about the old days.

title: Kutch Crafts Trail: journal, Bhuj to Nirona
paragraphs: Day 1, Bhuj. The Aina Mahal still carries the scars of the 2001 earthquake, but the hall of mirrors is luminous in the morning light. The palace was built for Rao Lakhpatji in the mid-eighteenth century, and its master craftsman Ram Singh Malam is said to have learnt glass-making and clockwork in Europe.

Day 2, Ajrakhpur. The Khatri families who moved here from Dhamadka after the earthquake still print ajrakh by hand. A single cloth passes through more than a dozen stages: scouring, resist printing with clay and gum, indigo baths and madder red. Printers like to explain 'ajrakh' as 'aaj rakh', keep it today.

Day 3, Nirona. In a courtyard, a Rogan artist drew a tree of life by pulling threads of boiled castor-oil paste from a metal stylus, never touching the cloth. Down the lane, copper bells were being hammered and baked in mud, the way the village has made them for generations.

title: Notes on Harappan water systems: Lothal and Dholavira
paragraphs: Lothal, morning. The great brick basin on the eastern edge of the town is 'the dockyard' in every guidebook, though archaeologists still debate whether it served as a dock or a reservoir. Standing at its edge, the estuary feels close; the sea was once nearer than it is today.

Dholavira, two days later. On Khadir island the city was planned around water: rock-cut reservoirs, stepped tanks and channels that caught every monsoon trickle from two seasonal streams. One reservoir has a flight of steps cut into the stone, an ancestor, perhaps, of the stepwells we have been chasing all month.

title: Notebook page 17: Rani ki Vav, third gallery
paragraphs:
पाटण, १५ जनवरी २०२४
रानी की वाव — तीसरी दीर्घा, उत्तरी दीवार

Patan, 15 January 2024
Rani ki Vav — third gallery, north wall

विष्णु के अवतार: वराह, नृसिंह, वामन और कल्कि।
एक नाग-कन्या की मूर्ति, बाएँ हाथ में दर्पण लिए।
नीचे के कुंड में पानी लगभग दो फ़ीट।

Avatars of Vishnu: Varaha, Narasimha, Vamana and Kalki.
A sculpture of a naga maiden holding a mirror in her left hand.
About two feet of water in the tank below.

title: Inscription notes copied at Adalaj
paragraphs:
અડાલજ, ૧૦ જાન્યુઆરી
પ્રવેશ મંડપના શિલાલેખની નોંધ

Adalaj, 10 January
Notes on the inscription in the entrance pavilion

સંવત ૧૫૫૫, માઘ સુદ ૫
વીરસિંહની રાણી રૂડાદેવીએ આ વાવ બંધાવી.
પાંચ માળ, ત્રણ પ્રવેશ સીડીઓ.

Samvat 1555, Magha Sud 5
Queen Rudadevi, wife of Veer Singh, had this stepwell built.
Five storeys, three entrance stairways.

title: Typed survey memo: Sidi Saiyyed jali screens
paragraphs:
HERITAGE SURVEY MEMO No. 7
Ahmedabad, 3 February 2024

Subject: condition of the western jali screens, Sidi Saiyyed Mosque (1572-73).
The intertwined tree with curling palm-like branches remains intact. Minor soot deposits on the lower panels; recommend dry brushing only. Photograph both screens at 10 a.m. for even light.
